p.seg: 46.13 The meaning of the village drinking ceremony [xiāng yǐn jiǔ]:
setting up the guest represents Heaven,
setting up the host represents Earth,
establishing the assistant and the associate represent the sun and moon,
establishing three guests represents the three luminaries.
The ancient practice of creating ritual
structures it with Heaven and Earth,
orders it with the sun and moon,
enriches it with the three luminaries;
it is the foundation of governance and education.
46.14 Boiling a dog in the east
is honoring the rising of *yáng qì* in the east.
Washing takes place at the eastern steps [zuò],
with the water basin to the east of the washbasin;
it honors the left sea of Heaven and Earth.
The vessel contains dark liquor [xuán jiǔ],
teaching the people not to forget their origins.
is to be one who observes and guards righteousness.
The north represents winter,
and the meaning of winter (dōng) is "middle" (zhōng),
and "middle" is to conceal.
Therefore, when the Son of Heaven is established,
he faces benevolence on the left (sacred),
they would first perform the Xiāng Yǐnjiǔ zhī Lǐ (鄉飲酒之禮, Village Drinking Ritual).
Therefore, the Yàn Lǐ (燕禮)
is that by which the righteousness between ruler and subject is clarified;
the Xiāng Yǐnjiǔ zhī Lǐ (鄉飲酒之禮)
is that by which the order of elders and juniors is clarified.

If virtue and conduct are established, then there will be no disasters of violence and disorder.

47.8 The meaning of "shooting" is "selection,"
or it can be said to mean "releasing."
"Selection" means,
he must first practice archery in the marsh.
The marsh
is where knights are selected.
After shooting in the marsh,
then one shoots in the archery palace.
Those who hit the target are allowed to participate in the sacrifice;
"A gentleman has nothing to contend for;
if he must contend, let it be in archery!
They bow and yield as they ascend [to the shooting platform],
and drink after descending;
such contention is that of a gentleman."
47.12 Confucius (Kǒngzǐ) said:
ministers, grand officers,
and gentlemen (士) who were deceased,
managed their regulations,
and their teachings and governance,
distinguished their ranks,
and rectified their positions.
the lord alone ascends and stands upon the mat,
facing west and standing apart,
signifying that no one dares to approach him casually.
48.3 The establishment of guest and host
is the ritual for drinking wine;
and he makes the steward be the one who offers the wine to the host.
The ruler must clearly illuminate the correct way to guide the people.
If the people follow this way and achieve merit,
then he takes only one-tenth of their gain.
Therefore, the ruler has sufficient resources, and the people are not impoverished.
Thus, superiors and inferiors are harmonious and affectionate, and do not resent each other.
Harmony and peace.
The Meaning of Betrothal
49.1 In betrothal rituals,
a duke of the highest rank has seven envoys,
a marquis or count has five envoys,
a viscount or baron has three envoys,
thereby clarifying nobility and commonness.
the guest has a private audience,
a private meeting,
provisions of cooked food and grain are presented,
*guī* and *zhāng* are returned,
gifts and presents are given,
banquets, meals, and feasts are held.
feeding the guests in their lodgings,
the implements for the five sacrificial animals are displayed inside,
thirty cartloads of rice,
thirty cartloads of grain,
the hay and firewood are double the grain,
all these are displayed outside,
the meat is dried,
but people are hungry and dare not eat it;
the sun sets and people are tired,
but they maintain reverence and solemnity,
correct their robes
and dare not become lax.
Used in victory in battle, there is no enemy;
used in rituals and righteousness, there is smooth governance,
externally without enemies,
internally with smooth governance,
this is called great virtue.
Therefore, the sage-kings value bravery, strength, and power.
sharp but not cutting,
this is yì 義 (righteousness);
when hung, it droops as if falling,
this is lǐ 禮 (ritual);
when struck, its sound is clear, resonant, and prolonged,
its end abruptly stops,
takes as its standard yin and yang,
accords with human feelings,
therefore it is called ritual.
Those who criticize it
do not understand how ritual arises.

yì duàn ēn. [righteousness cuts off kindness.]

ér jìng tóng, [and reverence is the same,]

Gù wèi jūn yì zhǎncuī sān nián, [Therefore, for a lord, one also wears the roughest mourning for three years,]
shows that there are not two superiors.
50.6 What is the staff for?
It is a symbol of rank.
The staff is given to the son on the third day,
to the *dàfū* on the fifth day,
and to the *shì* on the seventh day.
見無二尊也。 Seeing that there should not be two honored ones.
50.6 杖者何也？ What is the meaning of the staff?
爵也。 It is a symbol of rank.
三日授子杖， On the third day, a son is given a staff;
五日授大夫杖， On the fifth day, a Dàfū 大夫 is given a staff;
七日授士杖。 On the seventh day, a Shì 士 is given a staff.

老病不止酒肉。 The elderly and sick do not stop consuming wine and meat.
凡此八者， All these eight things,
以權制者也。 Are regulated by expediency.

恩之殺也。 It is the diminishing of affection.
聖人因殺以制節， The sage uses this diminishing to regulate the degree,
此喪之所以三年。 This is why mourning lasts for three years.
賢者不得過， The worthy cannot exceed it,

1.1. A. Wén Zhōngzǐ ******has written: 【0. 文中子 is the honorific posthumous name of WT. This text presents itself explicitly as a posthumous work. 1. This introduction 1.1.A is a written piece. It needs to be treated as concise learned composition rather than a discourse. 2. It reads very much like a very personal author's introduction to a 《續論語》envisaged by WT himself. 3.The frame of this is emphatic/emotional in both the initial and the final lines. 4. The question arises, to what extent the rest of the entries in this book are written compositions as opposed to reported dialogues.代考]

【直譯】還是究竟不算是言說呢？【總結】此處直譯以開放性質問作結，翻譯特色在於保持原文的思辨張力，餘韻悠長。

【直譯】還是究竟不算是言說呢？【總結】此處直譯以開放性質問作結，翻譯特色在於保持原文的思辨張力，餘韻悠長。【翻譯特色與特殊處理總結】此段翻譯以直譯為主體，約佔百分之八十五，嚴格對應莊子原文的哲理論證結構。特殊處理包括：約百分之十的概念明晰化，如「有始」譯為「宇宙開始的狀態」，既保持深度又增強可理解性；另約百分之五的句式節奏調整，如多重「未始」句式的層疊翻譯，再現原文遞進韻律。整體翻譯在維繫文言哲思的同時，注重現代讀者的認知習慣，成功平衡了學術性與傳播性。

【直譯】這就叫做含藏的光明。【總結】此句直譯「葆光」為「含藏的光明」，翻譯特色在於既直譯又揭示哲學意涵。【翻譯特色與特殊處理總結】此段翻譯以直譯為主體，約佔百分之八十五，嚴格遵循莊子原文的哲理論述結構。特殊處理包括：約百分之十的概念意象轉化，如「园而幾向方」譯為「圓融便接近道」，將抽象幾何關係轉為哲學表述；另約百分之五的文化負載詞處理，如「葆光」保留原意象並輔以「含藏的光明」闡釋。整體翻譯在維繫文言韻律的同時，注重現代讀者的理解需求，成功平衡了學術性與文辭典雅。

【直譯】所以寄寓於無竟。」【總結】「寓諸」譯為「寄寓於」，直譯動賓關係；以「無竟」收尾，凸顯道家終極歸宿。【翻譯特色與特殊處理總結】此段翻譯以直譯為主軸，力求在典雅文風中準確傳達莊子原意。整體而言，約百分之七十的內容採逐字對應策略，如「我不若勝」譯為「我不如你勝」，保留古漢語語序與結構，避免現代化扭曲。針對哲學專有術語，如「天倪」、「無竟」，百分之二十的處理採用直譯不釋義，維護學術純粹性，同時依賴讀者文化背景自行領悟。特殊調整佔百分之十，主要體現在語氣詞轉化，例如「邪」統一譯為「嗎」，以增強疑問句的流暢度，而不失古典韻味。此外，針對比喻性詞彙如「黮闇」，直譯為「昏暗」，既保留意象又避免過度闡釋，確保跨文化讀者能透過上下文理解深層寓意。總體而言，翻譯在直譯基礎上，兼顧漢語節奏與哲學深度，使莊子的相對主義與超脫思想得以清晰呈現。哲學總旨心得此段《齊物論》精闢闡發莊子核心哲思：其一，透過辯論的無效性，揭示真理的相對性與人類認知的局限，如「我與若不能相知也」直指主觀立場的偏狹，與現代詮釋學中「視域融合」概念相通，強調理解需超越二元對立。其二，「和之以天倪」提倡以自然之道調和矛盾，體現道家「無為」智慧，這不僅預示生態哲學的整體觀，更在當代衝突社會中啟發人們以包容心態面對分歧。其三，「忘年忘義，寓諸無竟」倡導超脫時空與道德執著，直指精神自由，與存在主義追求本真性相呼應，凸顯跨文化價值。總體而言，莊子以弔詭言說挑戰邏輯常規，非為否定理性，而是引領讀者躍升更高認知維度，在現代資訊爆炸時代，其思想尤具啟發性，敦促人們內省自覺，尋求心靈的寧靜與統一。

Outline:
To praise the virtuous and esteem morality
shines brightly for a thousand years;
to honor the root and respect the beginning
makes righteousness flourish from afar.
Chǔ Yuánwáng 楚元王 accumulated benevolence and established virtue,
opening up this border region;
his original customs and doctrinal achievements
served as a model for future generations.
The blessings of his lineage
truly enriched our humble clan;
his lingering fragrance and remaining influence
inspires throughout the ages.
Yet his burial mound is overgrown,
and his tomb is untended.
Remembering the distant past,
I sigh with lasting emotion.
It is said that because of love for the man who planted it,
the sweet pear tree was not cut down;
seeking to recognize the site of a tomb,
even Xìnlíng ìn Xìnlíng was not forgotten.
How much more so should we honor the origin
of the dynasty, the root of its foundation!
It is fitting to exempt five households near the tomb
from service and provide them with the perpetual task of sweeping and cleaning.
This should be implemented forthwith.

Principles:
To praise the worthy and revere virtue
shines brightly for a thousand years;
to honor the root and respect the beginning
makes righteousness flourish far and wide.
King Yuán of Chǔ accumulated benevolence and built a foundation of virtue,
opening up the borders of this land;
his pure character and virtuous deeds
set an example for future generations.
The blessings of his lineage
truly enrich our humble clan;
the fragrance of his legacy and the strength of his achievements
inspire hundreds of generations.
Yet the mound of his grave is overgrown,
and his tomb is untended.
Feeling for the distant past and preserving memories of what has gone by,
I sigh with endless contemplation.
To love the people is like cherishing a tree;
even the sweet pear tree should not be cut down;
in seeking out the abandoned graves,
even Xìnlíng cannot be forgotten.
How much more so should we care for the origin from which our prosperity springs,
the source from which our dynasty originates!
Five households near the tomb should be exempted from corvée,
and permanently assigned to sweep and maintain it.
This should be implemented immediately.
Outline and Principles:
To praise the virtuous and exalt moral character,
their brilliance will shine for a thousand years.
To honor the origin and revere the beginning,
the significance will naturally extend far.
Chǔ Yuán Wáng accumulated benevolence and established virtue,
opening up this territory.
His pure demeanor and virtuous deeds
served as a model for later generations.
The blessings of his lineage
truly enriched our humble clan.
His enduring fragrance and remaining influence
inspire for hundreds of generations.
Yet his burial mound is overgrown,
and his tomb is neglected and untended.
Reflecting on the distant past and preserving the memory of what has gone by,
I am filled with lasting sorrow.
When loving the people, one cherishes the trees;
even the sweet pear trees should not be cut down.
When seeking to honor a gravesite,
the memory of Xìn Líng should certainly not be forgotten.
How much more so should we care for the origin from which we have sprung,
and the source from which our dynasty began!
Let five families near the tomb be exempted from corvée,
and be permanently assigned to sweep and clean it.
This order should be implemented.

Wer wahren Wert nicht kennt,nimmt das Wichtige für unwichtig und das Unwichtige für wichtig.Wer das tut, wird aber in all seinen Handlungen notwendig Mißerfolghaben. Ein Fürst, der so handelt, wird zum Tyrann; einBeamter, der so handelt, wird zum Empörer; ein Sohn, der sohandelt, wird zuchtlos. Wenn in einem Staate auch nur eine vondiesen drei Menschenklassen vorhanden ist, so geht er sicher zugrunde,wenn er nicht großes Glück hat.
Wenn zum Beispiel eine Musik zwar angenehm zu hören ist,

aber durch ihr Anhören betäubt, so soll man sie gar nicht erst anhören.Wenn eine Gestalt zwar angenehm anzuschauen ist, aberdurch ihr Anschauen verblendet, so soll man sie gar nicht erst anschauen.Wenn eine Speise zwar angenehm zu essen ist, aberdurch ihren Genuß den Mund schal macht, so soll man sie gar nichterst essen. Darum verhält sich der Weise zu den Eindrücken derSinne des Ohres, des Auges und des Mundes also, daß er sie genießt,wenn sie dem Leben nützen, sie aber entbehrt, wenn sie demLeben schaden. Das ist der Weg zur Pflege und Vollendung desLebens.
Aber wie will ein zügelloser Mensch es machen, daßsein Leben nicht verdirbt?

Wenn 10000 Leute den Bogen ergreifenund gemeinsam nach einem Ziel schießen, so wird das Ziel sichergetroffen. Wenn 10000 Dinge gleißen und scheinen, um ein Lebenzu verderben, so wird dieses Leben sicher verderben. Wenn aberalles dazu mithilft, dieses eine Leben zu fördern, so wird diesesLeben sicher lange dauern. Darum richtet der Weise den Gebrauchaller Dinge so ein, daß sie sein vom Himmel gegebenes Lebenvollenden. Wer dieses Leben vollendet, dessen Geist kommt inHarmonie, sein Auge wird klar, sein Ohr verständig, sein Geruchfein, sein Geschmack scharf, und alle seine Glieder werden gewandtund frei. Ein solcher Mann findet Glauben, ohne zu reden, trifftdas Rechte, ohne sich vorher zu überlegen, findet sein Ziel, ohnesich vorher zu besinnen. Denn sein Geist durchdringt Himmel undErde, und sein Verstand um faßt das Weltall. Er steht den Dingenso gegenüber, daß alle zu seiner Verfügung stehen und ihm dienenmüssen; er gleicht darin Himmel und Erde. Ist er hoch drobenauf dem Königsthron, so wird er nicht stolz; ist er tief drunten alsgemeiner Mann, so wird er nicht traurig darüber. Von einem solchenMann kann man sagen, daß er seinen Charakter vollkommen gemachthat. Ehre und Reichtum ohne die Erkenntnis, daß Wohlhabenheitins Elend führt, ist schlimmer als Armut und Niedrigkeit.Denn wer arm und niedrig ist, dem fällt es schwer, die Dinge ansich zu raffen. Selbst wenn er Luxus treiben wollte, wie könnte5er's denn? Auf der Straße der Wagen und im Hause der Fahrstuhl,man sucht sie, um es sich selbst bequem zu machen, abersie heißen Maschinen zur Herbeiführung der Lähmung. FettesFleisch und alter Wein, man sucht sie, um sich selbst zu stärken, aberman heißt sie Gifte, die die Eingeweide faulen machen. Zarte Wangenund weiße Zähne und die verführerischen Töne von Tschongund We, man sucht sie, um sich selbst zu ergötzen, aber sie heißendie Axt, die das Leben fällt. Aber diese drei übel sind die Folgenvon Ehre und Reichtum. Darum gab es unter den Menschen desAltertums solche, die sich weigerten, geehrt und reich zu werden,weil sie das Leben wichtig nahmen. Wer sich nicht durch eitleNamen betören lassen will, sondern die Wirklichkeit wichtignimmt, der darf diese Mahnung nicht unbeachtet lassen.
Darum richtet der Weise den Gebrauchaller Dinge so ein, daß sie sein vom Himmel gegebenes Lebenvollenden.
Wer dieses Leben vollendet,

dessen Geist kommt inHarmonie, sein Auge wird klar, sein Ohr verständig, sein Geruchfein, sein Geschmack scharf, und alle seine Glieder werden gewandtund frei. Ein solcher Mann findet Glauben, ohne zu reden, trifftdas Rechte, ohne sich vorher zu überlegen, findet sein Ziel, ohnesich vorher zu besinnen. Denn sein Geist durchdringt Himmel undErde, und sein Verstand um faßt das Weltall. 养护生命并使它长成的是人。能够养护上天创造的生命而不触犯它，这样的人称作天子。天子的行为是把全面的爱护生命作为要务的。这是设立职官的原因。设立职官，是为了爱护生命啊。如今世上胡涂的君主，大量设立官职却反而因此妨害生命，这就失去了设立职官的初衰了。譬如制作武器,是用以防备强盗的。可是如今制作的武器反而用来攻杀自己，那就失去了制作武器的本来目的了。

与外物扰乱在一起，人就无法达到长寿。外物的作用，是用来供养生命的•，而不是用生命作代价去追求外物。可是如今世上糊涂的人大多以损耗生命去追求外物，这样作是不懂得轻重。不懂得轻重，就会把重的当作轻的，把轻的当作重的了。如果这样作,做每一件事都是要失败的。持这种态度做君主，就会迷乱乘背;做臣子，就会败乱国祸政;做儿子，就会狂妄无礼。国家只要有这三种情况中的一种，就必定灭亡，无可幸免。

万物众多繁盛，如果用以伤害一个生命，那么这个生命一定会被伤害的；如果用以滋养一个生命，那么这个生命一定会长久的。所以圣人统辖万物‘，是使生命获得善终的。身体不受损害，精神就和谐了，眼睛就明亮了，耳朵就灵敏了。嗅觉就敏锐了，口齿就伶俐了，全身的筋骨就通畅舒展了。像这样的人，不用表白就有信义，不用思虑就会合于实际，不用计算就有收获。他们的精神通达天地，覆盖宇宙。对于外物，他们无不承受，无不容纳，就像天地一样。他们上为天子而不骄傲，下为百姓而不忧闷。这样的人，可以称为德行完善的人。

Xìng (幸), is fittingly called "xìng" (幸).
Common people call xìng (幸) "jiǎoxìng" (僥倖) (lucky by chance).
When the Son of Heaven's carriage arrives,
the subjects receive his virtuous grace through "jiǎoxìng" (僥倖),
therefore it is called "xìng" (幸).
It is called the Heavenly Family.
"Jìn Zhōng" (禁中, the Forbidden Palace) refers to places where the gates are forbidden,
and those who are not attendants are not allowed to enter,
hence it is called "Jìn Zhōng".
Because the father of Empress Xiào Yuán (孝元) was Grand Marshal Yángpíng Marquis named Jìn (禁),
I dare not profanely mention the honorable title,
it is the meaning of respecting the king.
*Shèngyú* (imperial carriage) comes from the law.
The law states: "Dare to steal the *shèngyú* and clothing and accoutrements."
This refers to what the Son of Heaven wears and eats.
The Son of Heaven is supremely honorable,
Zhèn, that is I.
In ancient times, the noble and lowly shared it,
the honorable and humble did not avoid it,
so the meaning of using the same term was permissible.
Yáo said "Zhèn",
reigning for seventy years.
*Wángzhě zhìzūn*,
a different name for the four appellations.
*Wáng* is what those within the capital region call him;
the *wáng* possesses all under heaven,
therefore he is called *wáng*.
Cèshū (策書) (official documents written on bamboo or wooden slips),
cè (策) means "slips."
The *Lǐ* (禮) (rites) says:
"If it is less than one hundred *zhàng* (丈),
it is not written on *cè* (策) (slips)."
or being transferred to the capital,
the close ministers will state their official titles and full names.
If they are being dismissed or have committed a crime, their surname is omitted.
All *zhìshū* (制書) have a seal and an order token attached below,
and are sealed with the imperial seal regardless of distance.

"Sī Yī" (《絲衣》), one stanza of nine lines,
is the song used when dismissing the guest and the impersonator of the dead during sacrifices.

is used to announce the completion of the grand martial performance,
and speaks of the ability to imbibe the ways of the ancestors to nourish the world.
"Huán" (《桓》), one stanza of nine lines,
is the song used during military sacrifices, demonstrations of martial skills, and the parade before battle (lèi mà 類禡).

is the song used during the grand enfeoffment at the ancestral temple, bestowing rewards on the virtuous.
"Bān" (《般》), one stanza of seven lines,
is the song used during imperial tours of inspection to sacrifice to the Sì Yuè (四嶽) mountains, the Yellow River, and the seas.

Xu Kuangyi's commentary lists the crucial background:。荀文有：“鲁哀公问舜冠于孔子，孔子不对（杨惊注： ｀哀公不问舜德，徒间其冠，故不对也。＇）。三问，不对，哀公曰：寡人问舜冠于子，何以不言也沪孔子对曰；｀古之王者，有务而拘领（杨注：｀务，读为冒。拘与旬同，曲领也。，冒即｀帽＇）矣，其政好生而恶杀焉（杨注：｀言虽冠衣拙朴，而行仁政也。＇），是以凤在列树，麟在郊野，乌鹊之巢可附而窥也。君不此问而间舜冠，所以不对也。'“晏子文有：＂（齐）景公问晏子曰：｀吾欲服圣王之服，居圣王之室，如此则诸侯其至乎沪晏子对曰：｀法其节俭则可，法其服，居其室，无益也。三王不同服而王，非以服（服饰）致诸侯也……且古者尝有经衣挛领而王天下者，其义（当为｀政＇）好生而恶杀。'”.

Styles have ten thousand differences,
things have no single measure.
Although the distinctions are here,
They also prohibit evil and restrain license.
The essential is that words convey meaning and reasons are presented,
Therefore, there is no need for redundancy or length.
As things they are multifaceted,
Although the passage of time and what ceases are impermanent,
it is indeed difficult to make progress on a rough and uneven path.
If one can adapt to changes and understand the proper order,
it is like opening a channel to receive a spring.
If one misses the opportunity and meets [it] only later,
one is always grasping at the end to continue from the summit.
If one confuses the order of black and yellow (heaven and earth, the proper order),
then it will be murky and unclear.
Perhaps [a phrase] pushes upward and encroaches on the preceding clause,
or perhaps it reaches down and infringes on the following chapter;
perhaps the words are harmful, but the reasoning is similar,
or perhaps the words are smooth, but the meaning is obstructive.
If separated, they are both beautiful;
if combined, they both suffer.
Examine the best and worst with the smallest weight,
determine what to keep and what to discard with the finest hair.
If it is what the scales determine,
then it should certainly conform to the standard.
Perhaps the writing is complex and the reasoning rich,
but the meaning does not point to the right direction.
It reaches the point where there is no double meaning,

And so the many fragrant things gathered around them.
They mixed *shēn jiāo* with cinnamon,
How could they simply string together *huì* and *chǎi*?
Yáo and Shùn were upright and forthright,
Having followed the Way, they found the right path.
Why were Jié and Zhòu so unrestrained?
In the rows I planted *liúyí* and *jiēchē*,
Intermingling *dùhéng* and fragrant *zhǐ*.
Hoping their branches and leaves would grow tall and lush,
I wished to wait for the time when I would harvest them.
Even if they wither and die, what harm is there?
I grieve that all the fragrant plants are overgrown and neglected.
Though I cherish beauty and strive to restrain myself,
I am earnestly reproached in the morning and dismissed by evening.
Having dismissed me for my *huìxiāng*,
They further accuse me of embracing *lǎnchǎi*.
Yet these are the things my heart loves,
Though I die nine times, I shall not regret it.
Although I admire elegance and self-discipline
, I was forthright in my morning admonitions, only to be dismissed by evening.
Having dismissed me for my fragrant sachets of *huì*
, they further accused me of gathering *chǎi* plants.
Yet, it is what my heart deems good
, even if I die nine times, I would still not regret it.
I lament Líng Xiū's boundless ways
, never understanding the hearts of the people.
The many women are jealous of my beautiful eyebrows
, and spread rumors, slandering me as being wantonly licentious.
Indeed, the customs of the time are skillfully deceptive
, turning their backs on the compass and square to alter right and wrong.
They forsake the plumb line to pursue crookedness
, competing to be accommodating as the standard.
I am dejected and despondent
, I alone am in dire straits at this time.
I would rather die suddenly and wander away
, than bear to act in such a manner.
A raptor does not flock with others
, it has been that way since ancient times.
How can the square and circle accommodate each other?
How can those with different paths find peace together?
Bending my heart and suppressing my will
, enduring blame and pushing away disgrace.
Submitting my purity to die for uprightness
, has always been valued by the former sages.
I regret not examining the path properly
, I will pause and wait, for I am about to return.
I turn my chariot to retrace the road
, while I have not strayed too far from the path.
I walk my horse on the orchid bank
, ride to the pepper hill and rest there.
Advancement does not bring acceptance, only estrangement and blame,
I linger, waiting to turn back.
I turn my chariot around to return to the road,
While the straying is not yet too far.
I walk my horse on the orchid bank;
I will gallop to the pepper hill and rest there.
Entering without being accepted leads to blame;
Why are you so broadly outspoken and fond of self-cultivation,
uniquely possessing such admirable integrity?
Brambles and burrs fill the room,
yet you resolutely remain apart and do not wear them.
The masses cannot be persuaded one by one,
who will say they understand my innermost feelings?"
Tāng 湯 and Yǔ 禹 were solemn and respectful,
The Zhōu 周 dynasty discussed the Dao and made no mistakes.
They promoted the virtuous and appointed the capable,
Following the plumb line and ink marker without deviation.
August Heaven has no personal bias,
But selects and assists based on the virtue of the people.
But the sun hurriedly approaches dusk.
I order Xīhé to slow his pace,
Gazing towards Yānzī and not urging it on.
The road is long and stretches far,
I will go up and down to seek and search.
I let my horses drink in the Xiánchí,
Grieving that the high hill has no woman.
Suddenly, I wander in this spring palace,
Breaking off jade branches to add to my belt.
While the blossoms' glory has not yet fallen,
I will choose a fair maiden as a gift.
I order Fēng Lóng to ride the clouds,
I feared that Gāo Xīn 高辛 would be ahead of me.
Wanting to gather far away but finding nowhere to stop,
I idly floated around in carefree wandering.
Before Shào Kāng 少康 had a family,
I stayed with the two Yáo 姚 women of Yǒu Yú 有虞.
The arrangements were weak and the matchmaker clumsy,
They wear ài 艾 as filling in their belts,
Claiming that the secluded orchid is not fit to be worn.
They examine plants and trees, yet still cannot understand;
How can a beautiful jade be properly valued?
They spread dung and soil to fill the curtains,
Claiming that shēn jiāo 申椒 is not fragrant.
I fear the cuckoo will crow first,
Causing all the plants to lose their fragrance.
Why are my precious pendants suppressed,
Hidden by the obscurity of the masses?
It is only that these partisans do not trust me,
Fearing that they will be broken by jealousy.
Its fragrance is rich and difficult to diminish
, its scent still has not faded to this day.
I harmonize my measures to amuse myself
, I will drift and seek a woman.
When my adornment was at its peak
, I traveled and observed above and below.
I send forth numerous chariots to wait along the way.
I turn left at Mount Bùzhōu,
setting the Western Sea as my destination.
I encamp my thousands of chariots,
aligning the jade wheel covers and racing side by side.
I harness eight dragons, graceful and winding,
The qiú chime rings and the lín láng jingles.
On the jade mat are jade pillows,
Why not grasp the fragrant jade?
Fragrant dishes steamed on orchid mats,
Presenting cinnamon wine and pepper broth.
Raising the drumstick and striking the drum,
2.3 Xiāng Jūn The Goddess of the Xiang River
Jūn bù xíng xī yíyóu, My lord does not come, lingering indecisively,
jiǎn shuí liú xī zhōng zhōu? Whom does he keep waiting on the island?
Měi yàomiǎo xī yí xiū, Beautiful and elegant, fitting for adornment,
pèi wú chéng xī guì zhōu. Harness my cassia boat.
Qiúqiāng míng xī línláng. The jade pendants chime and the jade rings tinkle.
Yáo xí xī yù zhèn, Upon the jade mat are jade pillows,
hé jiāng bǎ xī qióng fāng. Why not hold a bouquet of exquisite flowers?
Huì yáo zhēng xī lán jí, Fragrant meat steamed, placed upon mats of orchids,
diàn guì jiǔ xī jiāo jiāng. We offer cassia wine with pepper liquor.
Yáng fú xī fǔ gǔ, Raising the drumsticks, we strike the drums,
shū huǎn jié xī ān gē, With slow and gentle rhythms, we sing peacefully,
chén yú sè xī hào chàng. The *yu* and *se* instruments are arrayed, grandly played.
Líng yǎn jiǎn xī jiāo fú, The spirits dance gracefully, in beautiful attire,
fāng fēifēi xī mǎn táng. Fragrant and lush, filling the hall.
Wǔ yīn fēn xī fán huì, The five tones mingle, a complex gathering,
jūn xīnxīn xī lè kāng. The lord is joyous, happy and at peace.
2.2 Yún Zhōng Jūn The Lord in the Clouds
Yù lán tāng xī mù fāng, Bathing in orchid-infused water, washing with fragrance,
huá cǎi yī xī ruò yīng. Adorned in splendid clothes, like a flower.
Líng lián quán xī jì liú, The spirit lingers gracefully,
làn zhāo zhāo xī wèi yāng. Shining brightly, endlessly.
Jiǎn jiāng dàn xī shòu gōng, I shall rest in the Palace of Longevity,
yǔ rì yuè xī qí guāng. Shining with the sun and moon.
Lóng jià xī dì fú, A dragon chariot and the attire of an emperor,
liáo áo yóu xī zhōu zhāng. Carefree I roam in circles.
Líng huáng huáng xī jì jiàng, The spirit descends majestically,
biāo yuǎn jǔ xī yún zhōng. Soaring far away into the clouds.
Lǎn Jì Zhōu xī yǒu yú, Surveying Jì Province, there is much to see,
héng sì hǎi xī yān qióng. Reaching across the four seas, how can one find an end?
Sī fū jūn xī tàixī, Thinking of my lord, I sigh,
jí láo xīn xī mēngmēng. Utterly weary, my heart is confused.
2.3 The Xiāng Jūn
My lord does not depart, lingering,
Whom do I detain on this mid-isle?
Beautiful and alluring, and fittingly adorned,
Luxuriantly I ride my cassia boat.
Interactions disloyal, resentment grows long,
Promises untrustworthy, telling me that he is not free!
At dawn, galloping swiftly along the riverbank,
At dusk, I halt my journey at the northern islet.
Birds perch on the roof,
Water encircles the hall below.
In the morning, I ride my horse swiftly along the riverbank,
In the evening, I cross over to the western shore.
I hear that my beloved is summoning me,
I will prepare my carriage to go with her.
I build a house in the water,
Thatched with lotus leaves.
Wide open is the gate of heaven,
Luxuriantly I ride upon dark clouds.
I order the whirlwind to lead the way,
And command the freezing rain to sprinkle dust.
The lord circles and descends,
Passing over the Kōngsāng mountain to follow you.
2.6 *Shǎo Sīmìng*
Autumn orchids and *míwú* (Selinum carvifolia)
Are arranged and grown below the hall.
Green leaves and white branches,
Their fragrant scent wafts over me.
The lady surely has her own lovely child,
Sūn alone is fit to be the people's guide.
2.7 Dōng Jūn
The sun is about to rise in the east,
Shining on my railing and the *fúsāng* tree.
I pat my horse and calmly drive on,
2.8 The Lord of the River
I travel with the goddess on the Nine Rivers,
A rushing wind rises, creating crosswise waves.
Riding a water chariot, carrying a lotus parasol,
Driving two dragons, with young dragons as outriders.
Ascending Kunlun Mountain, I look in all directions,
breaking off fragrant blossoms to give to the one I long for.
I dwell in the deep bamboo grove, never seeing the sky,
the road is treacherous and difficult, I alone come late.
Standing solitary on the mountain peak,
the clouds billow and are below me.
Deep and obscure, it seems daytime is darkened.
The wheels are mired, and the four horses are entangled.
We seize jade drumsticks and strike the sounding drums.
The heavens darken, and our majestic spirit is angered.
We sternly slay them all and abandon the plains.
We go out and do not return; we go forth and do not come back.
The level plain stretches endlessly, and the road is exceedingly long.
Māi liǎng lún xī zhí sì mǎ, I obscure the two wheels and tether the four horses,
yuán yù bāo xī jī míng gǔ. Grasping the jade drumstick, I strike the resounding drum.
Tiānshí zhuì xī wēilíng nù, Heaven's timing has failed, and its awesome power is enraged,
yán shā jìn xī qì yuán yě. Sternly slaughtering all, abandoning the fields.
Chū bù rù xī wǎng bù fǎn, Going out, never to return; departing, never to come back,
píngyuán hū xī lù chāo yuǎn. The plains are vast, and the road stretches exceedingly far.
Dài cháng jiàn xī xié Qín gōng, Wearing a long sword and carrying a Qín bow,
shǒu shēn lí xī xīn bù chéng. Though head and body are separated, the heart does not repent.
Chéng jì yǒng xī yòu yǐ wǔ, Truly, you are both brave and martial,
zhōng gāngqiáng xī bù kě líng. Ultimately strong and unyielding, you cannot be subdued.
Shēn jì sǐ xī shén yǐ líng, Though the body is dead, the spirit becomes divine,
zi hún pò xī wèi guǐ xióng. Your soul and spirit will be a heroic ghost.
2.11 *Lǐ Hún* (Summoning the Spirit)
Chéng lǐ xī huì gǔ, Completing the rites, gathering the drums,
chuán bā xī dài wǔ, Passing the *bā* and taking turns dancing,
kuā nǚ chàng xī róng yǔ. Beautiful women sing and dance gracefully.
Chūn lán xī qiū jú, Spring orchids and autumn chrysanthemums,
cháng wú jué xī zhōng gǔ. May it last without end, forever and always.

Jiǔ Zhāng Nine Declarations
4.1 Xī Sòng "Lamenting the Past"
Xī sòng yǐ zhì mǐn xī, Sorrowfully chanting to express my grief,
Fā fèn yǐ zhù qíng. Bursting with anger to give vent to my emotions.
Loyalty's name becomes more manifest? (zhōng míng mí zhāng?)
Nine Declarations
4.1 Lament for Sorrow
I regretfully chant to express my grief, (Xī sòng yǐ zhì mǐn xī,)
And give vent to my feelings with fervor. (fā fèn yǐ shū qíng.)
I think that no one is as loyal to the ruler as I am,
Yet I carelessly forget my humble and poor status.
I serve the ruler without duplicity,
But I am confused and do not know the path to favor.
What crime is there in loyalty that I should meet with punishment?
Therefore, the mouths of the masses can melt metal,
at first it seemed fine, but then I encountered danger.
Having been burned by hot soup, I blow on my vegetables;
why don't you change this intention?
Desiring to leave the stairs and climb to heaven,
you still have your former behavior.
I hold firm to my will and cannot bear to do it.
My back and chest are wounded with intersecting pain;
my heart is knotted with twisting sorrow.
I use tough magnolia to straighten fragrant orchids;
and gather fragrant Sichuan pepper to make provisions.
I sow *Jiānglí* 江離 and cultivate chrysanthemums;
I ride towards Èzhǔ and look back,
Sighing at the trailing wind of autumn and winter.
I walk my horse upon the mountain bank,
And rest my carriage by Fānglín.
I board a small boat and ascend the Yuán River,
As the rowers from Wú strike the water in unison.
Loyalty is not necessarily rewarded,
Virtue is not necessarily employed.
Wǔ Zǐ encountered misfortune,
Bǐ Gān was pickled into minced meat.
It has always been so in former times,
So why should I resent the people of today!
sorrowfully seeing the ruler and knowing that I will not see him again.
Looking at the tall *qiū* trees and sighing deeply,
my tears fall in a torrent like sleet.
Passing Xiàshǒu and floating westward,
I look back at Lóngmén but cannot see it.
My heart is lingering and grieving,
I did not know that Xià had become a hill,
Who can allow the two east gates to become overgrown with weeds?
My heart is not at ease for long,
Sorrow and worry follow one another.
Only the roads to Yǐng are distant and vast,
And the river and Xià are impossible to cross.
It is not my fault that I have been abandoned and banished,
how can I ever forget it day or night?
4.4 Chōu Sī (Drawing Thoughts)
My heart is filled with melancholy thoughts,
I can only sigh deeply and add to my sorrow.
My obstructed thoughts cannot be released,
Now I have exhausted my feelings to present my words,
but Sūn pretends to be deaf and does not hear.
Because I am truly not flattering,
the crowd indeed considers me a problem.
The clarity of what I first presented,
how can it now be uselessly lost?
it also has no good matchmaker by its side.
Its noble path is distant and daily forgotten,
and it wishes to declare itself but cannot.
It looks to the northern mountains and sheds tears,
it stands by the flowing water and sighs deeply!
Gazing at the short nights of early summer,
My worried heart is not fulfilled, to whom shall I tell these words?
4.5 *Huái Shā* (懷沙, Embracing Sand)
In the vastness of early summer,
the grasses and trees are luxuriant.
Grieving my heart with perpetual sorrow,
the blind think him without sight.
To change white into black,
to turn the top into the bottom.
The phoenix is in a cage,
while chickens and ducks soar and dance.
Jade and stone are mixed together,
Tāng and Yǔ are long past,
Distant and beyond admiration.
I restrain my anger and change my resentment,
Suppressing my heart and strengthening myself.
Separated from sorrow and not moving (changing my will),
I wish for my determination to have a form (manifestation).
I wipe away tears and stand gazing.
The matchmaker is cut off, the road is blocked,
words cannot be connected and sent.
The vexations of loyalty are endless,
stuck and unable to be released.
I state my innermost feelings from dawn onward,
and make an appointment with the Xūn Huáng people.
As spring begins and the year unfolds,
the white sun rises leisurely.
I will let my will wander and find pleasure,
following the Jiāngxià to amuse my sorrows.
Fearing to lift my skirt and wet my feet.
Ascending high does not please me,
Descending low I cannot.
Indeed, my form is not suited for it,
Yet I am hesitant and doubtful.
Broadly following my previous plan,
He banished his minister far away without a second thought.
Believing the slanderous flattery that muddied the waters,
He indulged his anger and went too far.
Why was the loyal minister without sin,
Yet subjected to defamation and blamed?
Ashamed of the sincerity and trustworthiness of the sunlight,
He sealed Mount Jiè and made it a forbidden area,
To repay his great virtue abundantly.
Thinking of the past intimacy with his person,
He mourned him in white silk and wept.
Some are loyal and faithful and die for principle,
While others are deceitful and arrogant and are not doubted.
Turning your back on the law and yet thinking to govern,
Is no different from this.
I would rather die suddenly and wander away,
Than fear the calamity will come again.
Without finishing my words, I will leap into the abyss,
Regretting that the foolish ruler does not understand.
4.9 *Bēi Huí Fēng* (Lament for the Whirling Wind)
The sorrowful whirling wind shakes the *huì* orchids,
My heart is full of grievances and wounded within.
Things that are small may perish,
Voices that are hidden may be the first to sing out.
Why did Péng Xián create such thoughts?
Throughout the long, endless night,
Concealing this sorrow, which will not depart.
Awake, I wander leisurely,
Briefly finding solace to rely on myself.
Sighing deeply with compassion and pity,
The sorrow within my heart cannot be stopped.
The road is distant and silent.
Entering the echo chamber where there is no response,
Hearing the reflections and finding nothing obtainable.
My sorrows are dense and unyielding,
Dwelling in grief that cannot be dispelled.
My heart is reined in and cannot find form,
I fear the roaring, echoing rapids,
Listening to the tumultuous sound of the waves.
The profusion of appearances has no order,
The vast wilderness has no record.
Crushed by the immensity, with nowhere to turn,
Rushing, shifting, where will I stop?
He repeatedly remonstrated with his lord, but was not heard,
so what use was it to weigh himself down with a stone?
My heart is entangled and cannot be untied,
and I think of Jiǎn Chǎn 蹇產, not releasing.
*Yuǎn Yóu* 遠遊 (Distant Excursion)
Indifferent and inactive, I am content.
I have heard of Chìsōng's (赤松) pure dust;
I wish to receive the wind of his bequeathed principles.
I value the excellent virtue of the True Person;
I admire the past generations' ascensions to immortality.
In the morning, I face the wind and express my feelings.
Gāoyáng (高陽) is distant and remote,
Where shall I proceed?
Repeatedly speaking:
Spring and autumn pass quickly and unhurriedly,
do not precede it with action.
The myriad things are formed thereby,
this is the gate of virtue."
Having heard of the ultimate nobility, I then depart,
swiftly, I shall set forth.
In the morning, I set forth from Tàiyí,
in the evening, I begin to approach the Mílü door.
I amass ten thousand chariots,
and they rush along in a swirling torrent.
I drive the graceful eight dragons,
I summoned Xuán Wǔ to rush and join me.
I had Wén Chāng follow behind to direct the journey;
I selected and assigned numerous gods to accompany our chariot wheels.
The road stretched long and far;
I slowly moderated my pace and raised my spirits high.
On the left, I had the Rain Master attend closely;
Xiānglíng was ordered to play the zither,
Hǎiruò was instructed to dance with Féngyí.
The dark dragons and other creatures came forth in procession,

The "Hàn Shū · Yìwén Zhì" (Book of Han, Treatise on Literature) under the Miscellaneous School states:
"《Shī Zǐ》, 20 chapters."
The "Zhì" (Treatise on Bibliography) of the Sui and Tang dynasties also say the same.
By the Song dynasty, the complete book was already lost.
Wáng Yīnglín's "Hàn Zhì Kǎozhèng" (Textual Research on the Treatise on Literature of the Book of Han) states:
"The 'Lǐ Shū Shūmù' (Bibliography of Lǐ Shū) preserved four chapters,
and the 'Guǎngé Shūmù' (Imperial Library Bibliography) only preserved two sections,
combined into one chapter."
None of these versions were passed down.
The versions that are circulated now
include the version of the Rèn family of Zhènzé, the version of the Huì family of Yuánhé, and the version of the Sūn family of Yánghú.
The Rèn version has a total of three sections,
named "Rén Yì" (Benevolence and Righteousness),
"Jūn Zhì" (Governance by the Ruler),
and "Guǎng Shì" (Extensive Explanation).
In reality, these are all gleanings of scattered texts,
forcibly attached to old titles.
